lore_anchors.definition: In Daoist cosmology, the Thirty-Six Heavens represent a layered celestial realm. In Desolate Era, it refers to a fusion of the Stargold Beads into thirty-six miniature major worlds, each comparable in size to the Grand Xia World.
A classification of magical treasure denoting supreme, perfected yang energy. These are among the most powerful artifacts in the Three Realms, typically left behind by True Gods or Daofathers.
A set of 3,600 beads that can be fused into 360 or 36 forms, ultimately manifesting as the Thirty-Six Heavens. An innate supreme-grade spirit-treasure originally owned by Daoist Threelives.
A colossal battle avatar formed from coordinated immortal cultivator formations, representing the concentrated might of hundreds of Celestial Immortals and Loose Immortals.
A second body cultivated by a Ki Refiner at the Primal Daoist stage; it shares the same soul and consciousness and can act independently.
The secret world of Patriarch Subhuti, which exists in a separate 'layer' of space, making it inaccessible to all standard travel and teleportation.
A natural, infinitely profound seal that manifests within primordial chaos; described as patternless and endless like the mathematical constant pi.
One of the Three Pure Ones, the highest deities in the orthodox Daoist pantheon. In Desolate Era, he is a top-tier cosmic power.
A top-grade Pure Yang treasure set consisting of bloodshadow formations, extremely well-suited for bat-type divine beasts.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What are the Thirty-Six Heavens in this context?
cultural_notes_faq.a: They are the supreme fusion form of Daoist Threelives' Stargold Beads, where thirty-six mini-major worlds are created, each comparable to the Grand Xia World in size.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does the artifact spirit change his attitude so quickly?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because fusing all 3,600 beads into the Thirty-Six Heavens is considered impossible for anyone below a True God or Daofather; Ji Ning's feat humbles the spirit.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Ji Ning leaving his Primaltwin and daughter behind?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He is entering a dangerous war zone and wants Brightmoon safe. The Primaltwin shares his consciousness and will guide her growth.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the 'Delegated Awe' trope at play here?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It's a Xianxia technique where a protagonist's power is measured by the reactions of legendary beings who failed where he succeeded, like Lord Laozi failing to fuse the Stargold Beads.
